points.title: 童年启蒙
points.description: 列奥纳多·达·芬奇出生于意大利托斯卡纳地区的芬奇镇，是私生子。他的父亲是公证员，母亲是农家女。这段时期，列奥纳多展现出对自然和艺术的浓厚兴趣，经常在乡村中观察动植物，绘制素描。这段早期经历培养了他敏锐的观察力和对细节的关注，为他后来的科学研究奠定了基础。父亲注意到他的艺术天赋，开始安排他接受正规教育。
points.descriptionEn: Leonardo da Vinci was born in Vinci, a town in Tuscany, as an illegitimate son of a notary and a peasant woman. During this period, Leonardo showed a keen interest in nature and art, frequently observing plants and animals in the countryside and sketching them. This early experience cultivated his sharp observation skills and attention to detail, laying the foundation for his later scientific research. His father noticed his artistic talent and began arranging for him to receive formal education.

points.title: 学徒时期
points.description: 14岁时，列奥纳多成为著名艺术家韦罗基奥的学徒。在韦罗基奥的工作坊中，他学习了绘画、雕塑和工程技术，并接触到当时佛罗伦萨的人文主义思想。这一时期，他参与了韦罗基奥的《基督受洗》等作品，画出了天使的左侧部分，展现出超越师傅的才华。1472年，他成为佛罗伦萨画家行会的正式成员。这段经历不仅提升了他的艺术技巧，也培养了他跨学科的思维方式和实验精神。
points.descriptionEn: At age 14, Leonardo became an apprentice to the renowned artist Andrea del Verrocchio in Florence. In Verrocchio's workshop, he learned painting, sculpture, and engineering techniques, and was exposed to the humanist ideas of Renaissance Florence. During this period, he participated in works like 'The Baptism of Christ', painting the left angel portion, showing talent that surpassed his master. In 1472, he became a master of the Guild of Saint Luke. This experience not only enhanced his artistic skills but also cultivated his interdisciplinary thinking and experimental spirit.

points.title: 米兰宫廷
points.description: 1482年，列奥纳多离开佛罗伦萨，前往米兰为斯福尔扎家族服务，担任军事工程师、建筑师、宫廷画家和设计师。这一时期是他创作的黄金时代，完成了《最后的晚餐》这一不朽杰作，并创作了《维特鲁威人》等著名作品。他还进行了大量科学研究，包括解剖学、光学和流体力学研究。在米兰，他设计了许多军事工程和城市规划方案，展现了他在工程学方面的才能。1496年，他开始记录笔记，形成了著名的《大西洋古抄本》，包含大量科学观察和发明设计。
points.descriptionEn: In 1482, Leonardo left Florence for Milan to serve the Sforza family as a military engineer, architect, court painter, and designer. This period marked his golden age of creation, where he completed the immortal masterpiece 'The Last Supper' and created works like 'Vitruvian Man'. He also conducted extensive scientific research in anatomy, optics, and fluid dynamics. In Milan, he designed numerous military engineering projects and urban planning schemes, showcasing his talent in engineering. In 1496, he began recording his notes, forming the famous 'Codex Atlanticus', containing numerous scientific observations and invention designs.

points.title: 辗转创作
points.description: 1500年，列奥纳多回到佛罗伦萨，在圣马可修道院工作，并创作了《蒙娜丽莎》的早期版本。1503-1506年间，他在佛罗伦萨创作了《安吉亚里之战》的壁画草图，并进行了大量解剖学研究。1506年，他再次前往米兰，为法国查理·安布瓦兹服务。1513年，他移居罗马，在美第奇家族的教皇利奥十世的支持下工作，但未能获得重要委托。这一时期，他继续科学研究，尤其是解剖学和光学，同时完善了《蒙娜丽莎》，这幅作品成为世界上最著名的肖像画之一。
points.descriptionEn: In 1500, Leonardo returned to Florence, working at the Monastery of San Marco and creating an early version of the 'Mona Lisa'. Between 1503-1506, he worked on the cartoon for the 'Battle of Anghiari' mural in Florence and conducted extensive anatomical research. In 1506, he went to Milan again, serving under Charles d'Amboise for France. In 1513, he moved to Rome, working under the patronage of Pope Leo X from the Medici family, but did not receive significant commissions. During this period, he continued his scientific research, particularly in anatomy and optics, while perfecting the 'Mona Lisa', which became one of the world's most famous paintings.

points.title: 晚年时光
points.description: 1516年，应法国国王弗朗索瓦一世的邀请，年迈的列奥纳多移居法国昂布瓦兹，担任国王的'第一画家、建筑师和机械师'。他在克洛·吕塞城堡度过了生命的最后三年，继续整理他的笔记和科学著作。在这里，他完成了《蒙娜丽莎》的最终版本，并创作了《圣约翰施洗》等作品。1519年5月2日，他在昂布瓦兹逝世，据传是在国王的怀抱中离世。法国国王称他为'伟大的天才'，并安排他安葬在昂布瓦兹的圣弗洛朗坦教堂。列奥纳多的晚年虽然远离意大利的艺术中心，但他的思想和作品对后世产生了深远影响。
points.descriptionEn: In 1516, at the invitation of King Francis I of France, the elderly Leonardo moved to Amboise, France, serving as the king's 'first painter, engineer, and architect'. He spent his final three years at the Château du Clos Lucé, continuing to organize his notes and scientific works. Here, he completed the final version of the 'Mona Lisa' and created works like 'St. John the Baptist'. On May 2, 1519, he died in Amboise, reportedly in the king's arms. The French king called him 'the great master' and arranged for him to be buried in the Saint-Florentin Church in Amboise. Although Leonardo's later years were away from Italy's artistic centers, his ideas and works had a profound impact on future generations.

appraisal.zh: 达·芬奇通常被视为文艺复兴“全才”的典范，其绘画成就与解剖学、工程学、流体力学等方面的探索共同体现了艺术与科学的贯通，笔记本与科学草图至今仍是研究文艺复兴科学思想的重要材料。不过也有研究者指出，他常因兴趣转移而留下大量未完成项目，解剖研究未系统出版，军事机械设计多停留于纸面，对赞助人的依赖也限制了其表达的自主。
appraisal.en: Leonardo is conventionally seen as the archetypal Renaissance man, whose painting and investigations in anatomy, engineering and fluid dynamics together embody the union of art and science, and whose notebooks remain key sources for Renaissance scientific thought. Yet some researchers note that his shifting interests left many projects unfinished, his anatomical work was never systematically published, his military designs remained largely on paper, and his dependence on patrons constrained his freedom of expression.

supporter.zh: 列奥纳多·达·芬奇被视为文艺复兴时期最完美的天才代表，他完美融合了艺术与科学，展现了人类创造力的巅峰。他的绘画技巧无与伦比，《蒙娜丽莎》和《最后的晚餐》等作品成为艺术史上的永恒经典。同时，他在解剖学、工程学、建筑学等多个领域的开创性研究，体现了他超越时代的远见卓识。达·芬奇的精神遗产在于他永不满足的好奇心和跨学科思维方式，激励后人打破学科界限，追求全面的知识和理解。
supporter.en: Leonardo da Vinci is regarded as the quintessential genius of the Renaissance, perfectly merging art and science and representing the pinnacle of human creativity. His painting techniques are unparalleled, and works like the 'Mona Lisa' and 'The Last Supper' have become eternal classics in art history. Meanwhile, his pioneering research in anatomy, engineering, and architecture demonstrates his visionary insights that transcended his time. Leonardo's legacy lies in his insatiable curiosity and interdisciplinary thinking, inspiring future generations to break down disciplinary boundaries and pursue comprehensive knowledge and understanding.

critic.zh: 批评者指出，达·芬奇虽然才华横溢，但缺乏专注力，导致许多项目未能完成。他的解剖学研究虽然深入，但未能系统化出版，影响了科学传播。此外，他的军事工程设计，如巨型弩和装甲车，虽然构思精妙，但缺乏实用性，更多是纸上谈兵。批评者还认为，达·芬奇对权威的妥协和对赞助人的依赖，限制了他思想的自由表达，使他的才华未能充分发挥。他的私生子身份也使他在当时的社会中面临一定的限制和歧视。
critic.en: Critics point out that although Leonardo was immensely talented, he lacked focus, resulting in many unfinished projects. His anatomical research, though profound, was never systematically published, hindering scientific dissemination. Additionally, his military engineering designs, such as giant crossbows and armored vehicles, though ingenious, lacked practicality and were more theoretical than functional. Critics also argue that Leonardo's compromises with authority and dependence on patrons limited the free expression of his ideas, preventing his full potential from being realized. His illegitimate status also placed certain limitations and discrimination on him in contemporary society.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，达·芬奇被定义为'文艺复兴人'的典范，象征着人类知识的统一性和创造力。他的笔记本和科学草图成为研究文艺复兴时期科学思想的重要资料。现代学者越来越重视他的科学贡献，认为他在解剖学、地质学和流体力学等方面的研究远超前于时代。在流行文化中，达·芬奇常被神秘化和浪漫化，成为'全能天才'的象征。然而，历史学家也努力还原一个更真实的达·芬奇，强调他作为艺术家、科学家和发明家的复杂身份，以及他所处的历史背景和社会环境对他的影响。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Leonardo is defined as the archetype of the 'Renaissance man', symbolizing the unity of human knowledge and creativity. His notebooks and scientific sketches have become important materials for studying scientific thought during the Renaissance. Modern scholars increasingly value his scientific contributions, recognizing that his research in anatomy, geology, and fluid dynamics was far ahead of his time. In popular culture, Leonardo is often romanticized and mystified, becoming a symbol of the 'universal genius'. However, historians also strive to present a more authentic Leonardo, emphasizing his complex identity as an artist, scientist, and inventor, as well as the influence of the historical context and social environment in which he lived.

self.zh: 学习艺术的最好方法是模仿自然。
self.en: The noblest pleasure is the joy of understanding.
